transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I'm here because I feel like I'm just coming apart at the seams. It really started when... well, ever since those foreclosure notices started coming in the mail. 

I just can't seem to handle it. I've been sitting out in my truck crying before work, and I jump every single time the phone rings. It's spilling over into my job, too. I'm snapping at the apprentices, and I keep making these stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never, ever would have made before. It's just getting to be too much to handle on my own.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time since you started getting those foreclosure notices?

I don't know if I'd really call it sad, or... or depressed. I mean, I'm not walking around feeling down in the dumps most of the time. It's more just... I don't know, it's just this massive weight. The crying is really just from being so completely overwhelmed by the whole mess with the house, not necessarily because I feel depressed, if that makes sense.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things other than the foreclosure notices?

No, not really. It's pretty much just the house. I mean, sure, I have the usual day-to-day stuff, but nothing that keeps me up at night or makes me jumpy like this. The foreclosure is the only thing that's really got me wound up this tight.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities because of the stress related to the foreclosure notices?

Yeah, I definitely have. It's... well, it's affecting pretty much everything right now. 

At work, they actually had to take me out of the high-risk repair bay because of those mistakes I mentioned. And outside of work, I've just stopped going to things. I used to volunteer at church, go to my fitness classes, and I even had these truck-club outings I always kept up with. But lately, I just... I don't show up anymore. I just can't bring myself to face anybody or do much of anything.
Have you been having any flashbacks related to the foreclosure notices?
No, nothing like that. I mean, I think about it a lot, obviously, but I'm not having flashbacks or anything. It's just a constant worry, not like I'm reliving it or seeing things.
Do you worry excessively about the foreclosure notices to the point where you think about it even when you're not trying to?

No, not really. I mean, like I said, it's on my mind a lot because it's a huge problem right now. But it's not like it just forces its way into my head when I'm trying to focus on something else. I just think about it because... well, because it's happening and I have to figure out what I'm going to do about it.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious most of the time. I mean, I'm definitely stressed about the house, and it's a heavy weight, but it's not like a constant, everyday anxiety where I'm panicked or anything. It's just a really bad situation that I'm dealing with.
Are you avoiding places or people because you're afraid they'll remind you of your foreclosure situation?

No, I'm not avoiding anything. I still go to work at the shop, see my friends, do my normal routine. I mean, I don't really want to talk about it with people, but I'm not hiding out at home or staying away from places just to avoid being reminded of it. It's just a financial mess I'm in, it's not something I'm scared of running into out in the world.
Do you feel like you're anxious most of the day, every day, because of the foreclosure situation?

No, not really. I mean, like I said, I'm definitely stressed out about it, but it's not like an all-day, every-day kind of anxiety. I'm not sitting around shaking or feeling panicked all the time. It's just... it's a huge problem I have to deal with, so it's stressful, but I wouldn't say I'm anxious all day long.
Has your stress about the foreclosure notices been affecting your relationships with family or friends?

Well, like I said earlier, I'm not avoiding people because I'm scared of talking about the house, but... I guess I have been dropping the ball on my social life just because of the stress. I've completely stopped showing up for church volunteering, my fitness classes, and the truck-club outings I used to keep up with. I just don't have the bandwidth for it right now. 

And it's definitely affecting my job, too. My boss actually had to take me out of the high-risk repair bay at work recently because my head's just not fully in it with everything going on.
Do you feel like you're on edge most of the time because of the foreclosure situation?

No, I wouldn't say I'm on edge. I don't feel... jumpy or keyed up, if that's what you mean. I'm not walking around with my nerves shot all day. Like I was saying before, it's more that I'm just really distracted and bogged down by the whole financial mess. But I don't feel wound up or on edge about it.
Have you experienced significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning as a result of your stress about the foreclosure notices?

Yeah, like I was saying just a minute ago, it really has. I mean... I've stopped doing pretty much all my normal stuff. I don't show up for my church volunteering anymore, I dropped my fitness classes, and I haven't gone to any of the truck-club outings I used to keep up with. And at work, it's the same thing—my boss had to pull me out of the high-risk repair bay because my head just isn't in it. So, yeah, it's definitely getting in the way of my normal life right now.
How long have you been feeling overwhelmed by the foreclosure situation?
It's been about four months now. Pretty much ever since those first foreclosure notices started showing up in the mail... that's when it all really started feeling like too much to handle.
Have you been having trouble sleeping due to worrying about the foreclosure situation?

No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I mean, I'm definitely distracted during the day, like I said, but when it's time for bed, I still sleep about the same as I always have. I'm not lying awake all night worrying about it, if that's what you mean.
Do you worry about things other than the foreclosure notices even when there's no apparent reason to worry about them?

No, not really. I mean... it's pretty much just the house. I don't really worry about random things if there's no reason to. It's just... all my stress is completely tied up in those foreclosure notices and what's going to happen with that.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there's no apparent reason to worry?
Like I just said, no. It's really just the house. I don't sit around worrying about other things for no reason. It's the foreclosure that's got me so stressed out, nothing else.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your work performance since the foreclosure notices started?

Yeah, I definitely have. It got bad enough that they actually took me out of the high-risk repair bay at work. I guess I'm just too distracted to be doing the heavy stuff safely right now. 

And it's really not just work, either. I've pretty much stopped showing up for everything else. I haven't been going to my church volunteering, my fitness classes, or even the truck-club outings I used to always keep up with. I just can't manage to do any of it lately.
Do you find yourself worrying about the future in general, even when there aren't any specific problems like the foreclosure notices?

I feel like we keep going over this. No, I don't. Like I mentioned before, I don't just sit around worrying about the future for no reason. If it wasn't for the bank trying to take my house, I wouldn't be worrying at all. It's really just this one massive problem that's ruining everything right now.
Do you think you would feel significantly better if the foreclosure situation were resolved?

Yeah, I really think I would. But right now, the foreclosure process still isn't resolved. I'm still dealing with all the deadlines and the constant calls from the bank, so... you know, this whole thing hasn't ended yet. I haven't had a chance to see how I'll feel after it's over, because I'm still right in the middle of it.
Do you think your stress and worry about the foreclosure would stop if the situation was completely resolved?

I mean, like I just said, yes, I really think it would stop. But the foreclosure process still isn't resolved yet. I'm still dealing with the deadlines and the calls from the bank, so... well, the stress hasn't continued past the end of the situation, because there hasn't been an end yet. I'm still right in the thick of it.
